get.description:
Starts the [Authorization Code grant](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1) at the [authorization endpoint](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.1). Redirect the User's browser to this endpoint. The User signs in, then approves or denies the request. 

Proof then redirects to your `redirect_uri` per `response_mode`, carrying `code` and `state` on approval or `error` and `error_description` on denial. Every redirect also carries [`iss`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9207#section-2), the issuer identifier of this authorization server. Compare it to `issuer` from `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and reject the response when they differ. Exchange the `code` at `POST /oauth/v2/token` within 10 minutes. 

An unknown `client_id` or an unregistered `redirect_uri` sends the User to a Proof-hosted error page. Redirected [errors](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.2.1) use `invalid_scope`, `invalid_target`, `access_denied` and `invalid_request`.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: A [redirect URI](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.1.2) registered on your OAuth application. Receives the authorization response.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Space-separated [scope](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3) values requested from the User. `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` lists the supported scopes.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: An opaque [`state`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-4.1.1) value, returned unchanged on the redirect.

parameters.name: response_mode
parameters.description: The [response mode](https://openid.net/specs/oauth-v2-multiple-response-types-1_0.html#ResponseModes) for the authorization response. Defaults to `query`. [`form_post`](https://openid.net/specs/oauth-v2-form-post-response-mode-1_0.html) returns an auto-submitting HTML form.

Location.description: URL of the Proof-hosted authorization flow.

registration_endpoint.description: URL of the [client registration endpoint](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-3). Present when Dynamic Client Registration is available.

jwks_uri.description: URL of the [JWK Set](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7517#section-5) holding the keys of the authorization server.

response_types_supported.description: Response types the authorization endpoint supports.

grant_types_supported.description: Grant types the token endpoint supports.

token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported.description: Client authentication methods the token endpoint supports.

token_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_values_s.description: JWS signing algorithms the token endpoint accepts for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) client assertions.

revocation_endpoint_auth_methods_support.description: Client authentication methods the revocation endpoint supports.

revocation_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_val.description: JWS signing algorithms the revocation endpoint accepts for `private_key_jwt` client assertions.

introspection_endpoint_auth_methods_supp.description: Client authentication methods the introspection endpoint supports.

introspection_endpoint_auth_signing_alg_.description: JWS signing algorithms the introspection endpoint accepts for `private_key_jwt` client assertions.

code_challenge_methods_supported.description: [PKCE](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636#section-4.2) code challenge methods the authorization endpoint supports.

client_id_metadata_document_supported.description: Whether the authorization server accepts [Client ID Metadata Documents](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-oauth-client-id-metadata-document), an HTTPS URL used as the `client_id`.

authorization_response_iss_parameter_sup.description: Whether authorization responses carry the [`iss` parameter](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9207#section-2) identifying this authorization server. Compare it to `issuer` before using the `code`.

get.description: Returns the [authorization server metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8414#section-2): the endpoints, grant types, scopes, response types, response modes, PKCE methods and client authentication methods this authorization server supports.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail about the error, for developers.

redirect_uris.description: [Redirect URIs](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.1.2) for the authorization endpoint. At least one is required.

client_name.description: Name shown to the User on the authorization page. Proof generates one when this is absent.

client_uri.description: URL of the client home page.

logo_uri.description: URL of a logo for the client.

contacts.description: Email addresses of people responsible for the client.

tos_uri.description: URL of the terms of service of the client.

policy_uri.description: URL of the privacy policy of the client.

jwks_uri.description: URL of the [JWK Set](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7517#section-5) of the client. Supply either `jwks_uri` or `jwks`.

jwks.description: The [JWK Set](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7517#section-5) of the client, by value. Supply either `jwks` or `jwks_uri`.

software_id.description: Identifier the client developer assigns to the client software.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: Requested client authentication method. `private_key_jwt` requires `jwks` or `jwks_uri` and issues no `client_secret`; any other value results in `client_secret_post`.

client_secret.description: The client secret issued to the client. Returned in this response only.

client_id_issued_at.description: Issue time of the `client_id`, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

client_secret_expires_at.description: Expiry of the `client_secret`, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. `0` marks a secret that lasts indefinitely.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: The client authentication method the client uses at the token endpoint.

grant_types.description: Grant types the client may use.

response_types.description: Response types the client may use.

scope.description: Space-separated [scope](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3) values the client may request.

redirect_uris.description: Redirect URIs registered for the client.

post.description:
Registers an OAuth client from the [client metadata](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-2) in the request body and returns a [client information response](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-3.2.1). The endpoint is unauthenticated. 

The `client_secret` appears in this response only. Proof sets `grant_types`, `response_types` and `scope`, and sets `token_endpoint_auth_method` to `client_secret_post` unless the request asks for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) with a `jwks` or `jwks_uri`, in which case no `client_secret` is issued.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail about the error, for developers.

scope.description: [Scope](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3) values granted to the access token.

expires_in.description: Remaining access token lifetime, in seconds.

uid.description: The [`client_id`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.2) the access token was issued to.

created_at.description: Issue time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

iss.description: The [`iss`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.1) claim: the authorization server that issued the access token.

aud.description: The [`aud`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.3) claim: the protected resource the access token was issued for. Present for resource-bound access tokens.

sub.description: The [`sub`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.2) claim: the subject the access token was issued for.

email.description: Email address of the User the access token was issued for. Returned when the granted scopes cover it.

given_name.description: First name of the User the access token was issued for. Returned when the granted scopes cover it.

family_name.description: Last name of the User the access token was issued for. Returned when the granted scopes cover it.

get.description: Returns the scopes, remaining lifetime and OAuth application of the [access token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.4) presented as a [Bearer token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1).

error_description.description: Human-readable detail about the error, for developers.

client_secret.description: Your client secret, for [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) client authentication.

client_assertion.description: A JWT signed with one of your registered keys, for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) client authentication: `iss` and `sub` are your `client_id`, `aud` is the issuer or the token endpoint URL, with `exp` and a single-use `jti`.

code.description: The [authorization code](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.3.1) returned to your `redirect_uri`. Valid for 10 minutes and a single exchange.

code_verifier.description: The [PKCE code verifier](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7636#section-4.1) matching the `code_challenge` sent to the authorization endpoint.

client_secret.description: Your client secret, for [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) client authentication.

client_assertion.description: A JWT signed with one of your registered keys, for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) client authentication: `iss` and `sub` are your `client_id`, `aud` is the issuer or the token endpoint URL, with `exp` and a single-use `jti`.

refresh_token.description: The [refresh token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.5) issued with a previous access token.

client_secret.description: Your client secret, for [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) client authentication.

client_assertion.description: A JWT signed with one of your registered keys, for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) client authentication: `iss` and `sub` are your `client_id`, `aud` is the issuer or the token endpoint URL, with `exp` and a single-use `jti`.

scope.description: Space-separated [scope](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3) values granted to the access token.

created_at.description: Issue time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

refresh_token.description: A [refresh token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.5), for grants that support refreshing.

post.description: Issues an [access token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.4) from the [token endpoint](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.2). Client authentication uses [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1), [`client_secret_basic`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) or [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2). `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` lists the supported grant types.

example.error_description: The requested scope is invalid, unknown, or malformed.
Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method.

error_description.description: Human-readable detail about the error, for developers.

token.description: The access token or refresh token to revoke, issued to the authenticated client.

client_secret.description: Your client secret, for [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) client authentication.

client_assertion.description: A JWT signed with one of your registered keys, for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) client authentication: `iss` and `sub` are your `client_id`, `aud` is the issuer or the token endpoint URL, with `exp` and a single-use `jti`.

post.description: Revokes an [access token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.4) or [refresh token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-1.5) issued to the authenticated client, per [RFC 7009](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7009). Client authentication uses [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1), [`client_secret_basic`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) or [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2). Responds 200 for a revoked token and for an unknown token.

example.error_description: You are not authorized to revoke this token

error_description.description: Human-readable detail about the error, for developers.

client_secret.description: Your client secret, for [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1) client authentication.

client_assertion.description: A JWT signed with one of your registered keys, for [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) client authentication: `iss` and `sub` are your `client_id`, `aud` is the issuer or the token endpoint URL, with `exp` and a single-use `jti`.

active.description: Whether the token is currently active, per the [introspection response](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7662#section-2.2). `false` stands alone.

scope.description: Space-separated [scope](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-3.3) values granted to the token.

client_id.description: The [`client_id`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.2) the token was issued to.

iat.description: The [`iat`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.6) claim: issue time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

exp.description: The [`exp`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.4) claim: expiry, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Present for tokens that expire.

iss.description: The [`iss`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.1) claim: the authorization server that issued the token.

aud.description: The [`aud`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.3) claim: the protected resource the token was issued for. Present for resource-bound tokens.

sub.description: The [`sub`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7519#section-4.1.2) claim: the subject the token was issued for.

post.description: Returns the state of a token, per [RFC 7662](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7662). Callers authenticate as the client the token was issued to, or as the protected resource the token was issued for, with [`client_secret_post`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1), [`client_secret_basic`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6749#section-2.3.1), [`private_key_jwt`](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7523#section-2.2) or a [Bearer token](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6750#section-2.1). Expired, revoked and unknown tokens return `active: false`.

example.error_description: Client authentication failed due to unknown client, no client authentication included, or unsupported authentication method.
